This wrapper is then stored directly via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`, so the credential key becomes the Zod result object instead of the parsed credentials, corrupting stored credentials and breaking later Google API calls.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the code now does `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and then persists it via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. But `parseRefreshTokenResponse` (new file `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`) returns the Zod `safeParse` result object (with `{ success, data, error }`), not the parsed credential data itself (`.data`). This would store the wrapper object into `credential.key` instead of the actual credential payload, corrupting stored credentials and likely breaking subsequent Google API usage.
